newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish court sentences editor over EU diary.
newsitem.headline: Danish court sentences editor over EU diary.

text.p: Danish magistrates on Friday gave a suspended 20-day prison sentence to a leading newspaper editor for publishing EU Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard's diary without her consent, a court official told Reuters.

Prosecutors had demanded six months jail for Politiken's Toeger Seidenfaden, who in October 1995 published Bjerregaard's diary in a 20-page supplement after she pledged publicly not to publish the book, with its unflattering references to European leaders.
Seidenfaden said he had Bjerregaard's "silent acquiescence" in publishing the undiplomatic diary, an assertion denied by the author, the European Commissioner for environmental affairs.
"The Commissioner's Diary" caused a row at home and abroad for its barbed descriptions of French President Jacques Chirac, Germany's Helmut Kohl and former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez.
She said Chirac was a man of limited stature, unlikely to grow in his post, Kohl was offhand and inattentive and Gonzalez lacked energy and political will.
Seidenfaden said he would challenge the conviction.
"I intend to appeal the ruling to the High Court," he told Reuters.
"I am of course very happy that the court only sentenced me to a 20-day suspended prison sentence when the prosecution asked for an unconditional six months at the minimum," he said.

No date has yet been set for a civil case in which Bjerregaard and her publishers Aschehoug are claiming 6.5 million crowns ($1 million) from Seidenfaden and Politiken for breach of copyright. ($ = 6.484 Danish Crowns)
